problems.title: A calmer afternoon at the neighborhood library
problems.problem: A small library becomes crowded during afternoon pickups and returns. It has a request sheet, adjustable pickup windows, a few trained helpers, labeled shelves, and enough room to separate several activities. Staff want a practical plan that preserves walk-in access. Each decision below concerns a different part of the service; none requires exclusive use of all helpers or space.
problems.goal: Keep books moving and make the afternoon service easier to use without excluding readers who arrive without an appointment.

decisions.question: How should readers and staff agree on pickup windows?
decisions.context: Readers can give preferences on a shared request sheet, and staff can reserve space in several pickup windows.

options.mechanism: Readers rank pickup windows on the request sheet before staff reserve shelf space.
options.consequence: Staff can use those preferences to spread pickups across the available windows.
options.application: Readers rank pickup windows on the request sheet before staff reserve shelf space. Staff can use those preferences to spread pickups across the available windows.

options.mechanism: Staff propose pickup windows on the request sheet before readers confirm or request a change.
options.consequence: The initial spread comes from staff, with reader preferences correcting unsuitable assignments.
options.application: Staff propose pickup windows on the request sheet before readers confirm or request a change. The initial spread comes from staff, with reader preferences correcting unsuitable assignments.

options.mechanism: Readers claim pickup windows on the request sheet while staff reserve shelf space as claims arrive.
options.consequence: The available spaces limit crowding as readers make their own choices.
options.application: Readers claim pickup windows on the request sheet while staff reserve shelf space as claims arrive. The available spaces limit crowding as readers make their own choices.

decisions.question: Who should choose when a requested book is prepared?
decisions.context: A preparation list shows each requested book, its reader, and its agreed pickup window.

options.mechanism: Staff prepare each requested book shortly before its pickup window, following the preparation list.
options.consequence: Shelf space remains available for books whose readers are arriving soon.
options.application: Staff prepare each requested book shortly before its pickup window, following the preparation list. Shelf space remains available for books whose readers are arriving soon.

options.mechanism: Helpers prepare the requested books in one early pass, and staff use the preparation list to group them by pickup window.
options.consequence: The desk avoids repeated preparation during the afternoon rush.
options.application: Helpers prepare the requested books in one early pass, and staff use the preparation list to group them by pickup window. The desk avoids repeated preparation during the afternoon rush.

options.mechanism: Readers confirm they are on their way, and staff then prepare the requested books from the preparation list.
options.consequence: Preparation effort follows readers who are likely to collect soon.
options.application: Readers confirm they are on their way, and staff then prepare the requested books from the preparation list. Preparation effort follows readers who are likely to collect soon.

decisions.question: How should a reader announce arrival?
decisions.context: The entrance has an arrival sheet, and the pickup desk can see it without leaving its station.

options.mechanism: Readers add their names to the arrival sheet, and the pickup desk calls them when their books are ready.
options.consequence: Readers can wait away from the desk until called.
options.application: Readers add their names to the arrival sheet, and the pickup desk calls them when their books are ready. Readers can wait away from the desk until called.

options.mechanism: The pickup desk adds names to the arrival sheet after briefly greeting each reader.
options.consequence: A short personal check records arrivals before readers move aside.
options.application: The pickup desk adds names to the arrival sheet after briefly greeting each reader. A short personal check records arrivals before readers move aside.

options.mechanism: A helper gathers names from arriving readers and carries the arrival sheet to the pickup desk at regular intervals.
options.consequence: The desk receives grouped arrival updates without a continuous line of introductions.
options.application: A helper gathers names from arriving readers and carries the arrival sheet to the pickup desk at regular intervals. The desk receives grouped arrival updates without a continuous line of introductions.

decisions.question: How should walk-ins share the pickup desk with booked readers?
decisions.context: The desk serves both booked readers and walk-ins, and staff can divide its working time into short service blocks.

options.mechanism: Staff alternate short service blocks between booked readers and walk-ins at the pickup desk.
options.consequence: Both groups receive a regular turn even when the other group is busy.
options.application: Staff alternate short service blocks between booked readers and walk-ins at the pickup desk. Both groups receive a regular turn even when the other group is busy.

options.mechanism: Staff reserve an initial portion of each service block for booked readers and use the remainder for walk-ins.
options.consequence: Booked arrivals have predictable access while walk-ins use the continuing spare time.
options.application: Staff reserve an initial portion of each service block for booked readers and use the remainder for walk-ins. Booked arrivals have predictable access while walk-ins use the continuing spare time.

options.mechanism: Staff begin each service block with the longer waiting group, whether booked readers or walk-ins.
options.consequence: Service follows the greater current wait instead of a fixed group order.
options.application: Staff begin each service block with the longer waiting group, whether booked readers or walk-ins. Service follows the greater current wait instead of a fixed group order.

decisions.question: How should quick questions be separated from book collection?
decisions.context: A question pad is available beside the pickup desk, and a helper can answer routine questions.

options.mechanism: Readers write routine questions on the pad, and the helper answers them while staff handle book collection.
options.consequence: Questions can be addressed without interrupting each collection.
options.application: Readers write routine questions on the pad, and the helper answers them while staff handle book collection. Questions can be addressed without interrupting each collection.

options.mechanism: The helper asks waiting readers for routine questions and writes answers on the pad before they reach the pickup desk.
options.consequence: Common issues can be settled during the wait rather than at collection.
options.application: The helper asks waiting readers for routine questions and writes answers on the pad before they reach the pickup desk. Common issues can be settled during the wait rather than at collection.

options.mechanism: Staff finish each book collection before noting any remaining routine question on the pad for the helper.
options.consequence: The collection transaction stays short while a separate follow-up remains available.
options.application: Staff finish each book collection before noting any remaining routine question on the pad for the helper. The collection transaction stays short while a separate follow-up remains available.

decisions.question: How should shelf labels help staff locate requested books?
decisions.context: Requested books can be grouped on several shelves, and labels can show either a reader name or a pickup window.

options.mechanism: Staff group requested books by pickup window and add reader names within each shelf label.
options.consequence: The time grouping narrows the search before staff check a name.
options.application: Staff group requested books by pickup window and add reader names within each shelf label. The time grouping narrows the search before staff check a name.

options.mechanism: Staff group requested books by reader name and add pickup windows within each shelf label.
options.consequence: The name grouping narrows the search while the window remains visible.
options.application: Staff group requested books by reader name and add pickup windows within each shelf label. The name grouping narrows the search while the window remains visible.

options.mechanism: Staff assign a shelf location to each requested book and put that location beside both reader name and pickup window on a desk list.
options.consequence: The desk list directs the search without sorting the shelves by either field.
options.application: Staff assign a shelf location to each requested book and put that location beside both reader name and pickup window on a desk list. The desk list directs the search without sorting the shelves by either field.

decisions.question: What should happen when a reader misses a pickup window?
decisions.context: A missed pickup can be held for one more service period, and the reader can be contacted.

options.mechanism: Staff contact the reader to agree on a new pickup window before moving the book to the next period’s holding shelf.
options.consequence: The extra hold follows a confirmed intention to collect.
options.application: Staff contact the reader to agree on a new pickup window before moving the book to the next period’s holding shelf. The extra hold follows a confirmed intention to collect.

options.mechanism: Staff move the book to the next period’s holding shelf and then contact the reader with the new pickup window.
options.consequence: The book remains available while the reader receives a default second opportunity.
options.application: Staff move the book to the next period’s holding shelf and then contact the reader with the new pickup window. The book remains available while the reader receives a default second opportunity.

options.mechanism: Staff contact the reader with the remaining pickup windows and move the book only after the reader selects one.
options.consequence: The reader chooses among the remaining spaces before the extra hold is arranged.
options.application: Staff contact the reader with the remaining pickup windows and move the book only after the reader selects one. The reader chooses among the remaining spaces before the extra hold is arranged.

decisions.question: How should a returned book enter the checking queue?
decisions.context: Returned books need a brief condition check, and a return slip can record the book and its arrival.

options.mechanism: Readers place returned books beside completed return slips, and helpers check them in arrival order.
options.consequence: The slips preserve order without requiring a separate intake conversation.
options.application: Readers place returned books beside completed return slips, and helpers check them in arrival order. The slips preserve order without requiring a separate intake conversation.

options.mechanism: Helpers accept returned books and complete the return slips during a brief intake conversation.
options.consequence: Questions about a return are resolved before it enters the checking queue.
options.application: Helpers accept returned books and complete the return slips during a brief intake conversation. Questions about a return are resolved before it enters the checking queue.

options.mechanism: Readers hand over returned books, and helpers complete return slips during periodic grouped checks.
options.consequence: The handover stays quick while recording and checking happen together later.
options.application: Readers hand over returned books, and helpers complete return slips during periodic grouped checks. The handover stays quick while recording and checking happen together later.

decisions.question: How should checked returns be reshelved?
decisions.context: Checked returns are placed on a trolley, and helpers can sort by shelf location or by the age of the return.

options.mechanism: Helpers sort the trolley by shelf location and reshelve each location’s checked returns together.
options.consequence: Each shelving trip covers a compact part of the library.
options.application: Helpers sort the trolley by shelf location and reshelve each location’s checked returns together. Each shelving trip covers a compact part of the library.

options.mechanism: Helpers take the oldest checked returns from the trolley first and follow their shelf locations.
options.consequence: Books waiting longest become available again first.
options.application: Helpers take the oldest checked returns from the trolley first and follow their shelf locations. Books waiting longest become available again first.

options.mechanism: Helpers divide checked returns into small trolley batches and sort each batch by shelf location before shelving it.
options.consequence: Short batches balance prompt return with compact shelving trips.
options.application: Helpers divide checked returns into small trolley batches and sort each batch by shelf location before shelving it. Short batches balance prompt return with compact shelving trips.

decisions.question: How should a book move between the preparation area and the desk?
decisions.context: A transfer tray and a written transfer list can connect book preparation with the pickup desk.

options.mechanism: Preparation helpers fill the transfer tray and send it with a list after a small batch is ready.
options.consequence: The desk receives books and their records together in grouped deliveries.
options.application: Preparation helpers fill the transfer tray and send it with a list after a small batch is ready. The desk receives books and their records together in grouped deliveries.

options.mechanism: Desk staff send a transfer list for the readers currently waiting, and preparation helpers fill the tray to match it.
options.consequence: Transfers follow immediate pickup demand.
options.application: Desk staff send a transfer list for the readers currently waiting, and preparation helpers fill the tray to match it. Transfers follow immediate pickup demand.

options.mechanism: A helper carries the transfer tray at fixed intervals and checks the written list at both ends.
options.consequence: Regular rounds connect the two areas without repeated individual requests.
options.application: A helper carries the transfer tray at fixed intervals and checks the written list at both ends. Regular rounds connect the two areas without repeated individual requests.

decisions.question: How should readers request extra assistance?
decisions.context: Some readers prefer help carrying or locating books, and a helper can provide it without requiring a reason.

options.mechanism: Readers request assistance when choosing a pickup window, and staff place the request on the helper’s list.
options.consequence: The helper can be available when those readers arrive.
options.application: Readers request assistance when choosing a pickup window, and staff place the request on the helper’s list. The helper can be available when those readers arrive.

options.mechanism: A helper offers assistance at arrival and records accepted requests on a list.
options.consequence: Readers can choose help after seeing what they need that day.
options.application: A helper offers assistance at arrival and records accepted requests on a list. Readers can choose help after seeing what they need that day.

options.mechanism: Staff offer assistance at collection and pass accepted requests to the helper’s list.
options.consequence: Help is offered at the point where carrying or locating difficulties become clear.
options.application: Staff offer assistance at collection and pass accepted requests to the helper’s list. Help is offered at the point where carrying or locating difficulties become clear.

decisions.question: How should a reader hear about a temporary delay?
decisions.context: Staff can update a delay notice and speak with readers whose pickup is affected.

options.mechanism: Staff update the delay notice first and then speak with affected readers who want an individual update.
options.consequence: A common message reaches everyone before personal follow-up.
options.application: Staff update the delay notice first and then speak with affected readers who want an individual update. A common message reaches everyone before personal follow-up.

options.mechanism: Staff speak with affected readers first and then update the delay notice with the shared explanation.
options.consequence: The notice reflects the questions raised in those conversations.
options.application: Staff speak with affected readers first and then update the delay notice with the shared explanation. The notice reflects the questions raised in those conversations.

options.mechanism: A helper keeps the delay notice current while staff speak with affected readers at the same time.
options.consequence: Shared and individual updates proceed without waiting for one another.
options.application: A helper keeps the delay notice current while staff speak with affected readers at the same time. Shared and individual updates proceed without waiting for one another.

decisions.question: How should feedback be gathered without slowing departures?
decisions.context: A short feedback card and a nearby collection box are available for readers leaving the service.

options.mechanism: Staff hand readers a feedback card at collection and invite them to place it in the box on the way out.
options.consequence: Readers can respond after the transaction has finished.
options.application: Staff hand readers a feedback card at collection and invite them to place it in the box on the way out. Readers can respond after the transaction has finished.

options.mechanism: A helper offers feedback cards near the exit and points readers to the collection box.
options.consequence: The pickup desk does not need to introduce the feedback request.
options.application: A helper offers feedback cards near the exit and points readers to the collection box. The pickup desk does not need to introduce the feedback request.

options.mechanism: Readers take feedback cards from a stand beside the collection box after seeing a brief invitation near the exit.
options.consequence: Feedback remains self-directed and separate from staff interactions.
options.application: Readers take feedback cards from a stand beside the collection box after seeing a brief invitation near the exit. Feedback remains self-directed and separate from staff interactions.

decisions.question: How should helpers hand over unfinished tasks?
decisions.context: Helpers overlap briefly at a shift change and can use a shared list of unfinished tasks.

options.mechanism: The outgoing helper writes the unfinished-task list before the overlap and explains it to the incoming helper.
options.consequence: The handover starts from a prepared record.
options.application: The outgoing helper writes the unfinished-task list before the overlap and explains it to the incoming helper. The handover starts from a prepared record.

options.mechanism: The incoming helper reviews the work during the overlap and writes the unfinished-task list with the outgoing helper.
options.consequence: The new helper checks understanding while the record is made.
options.application: The incoming helper reviews the work during the overlap and writes the unfinished-task list with the outgoing helper. The new helper checks understanding while the record is made.

options.mechanism: Both helpers mark unfinished tasks on the shared list as they occur, then review only unresolved entries during the overlap.
options.consequence: The handover focuses on work that still needs attention.
options.application: Both helpers mark unfinished tasks on the shared list as they occur, then review only unresolved entries during the overlap. The handover focuses on work that still needs attention.

decisions.question: How should the library encourage quieter waiting?
decisions.context: Readers can wait in several spots, and a quiet-waiting notice can be moved around the pickup area.

options.mechanism: Staff place the quiet-waiting notice beside the waiting spots before the service starts.
options.consequence: Readers encounter the expectation as they choose where to wait.
options.application: Staff place the quiet-waiting notice beside the waiting spots before the service starts. Readers encounter the expectation as they choose where to wait.

options.mechanism: A helper points out quieter waiting spots and then places the notice where readers have gathered.
options.consequence: The reminder follows the actual waiting pattern.
options.application: A helper points out quieter waiting spots and then places the notice where readers have gathered. The reminder follows the actual waiting pattern.

options.mechanism: Staff place the notice at the entrance with a simple map of quieter waiting spots.
options.consequence: Readers can choose a suitable place before reaching the crowded desk.
options.application: Staff place the notice at the entrance with a simple map of quieter waiting spots. Readers can choose a suitable place before reaching the crowded desk.

decisions.question: How should staff choose one improvement for the next afternoon?
decisions.context: The team has a wait log, reader feedback, and a short closing discussion.

options.mechanism: Staff identify the longest waits in the log and use reader feedback to choose one improvement during closing.
options.consequence: The improvement begins with a measured bottleneck and checks its effect on readers.
options.application: Staff identify the longest waits in the log and use reader feedback to choose one improvement during closing. The improvement begins with a measured bottleneck and checks its effect on readers.

options.mechanism: Staff identify the most repeated concern in reader feedback and check the wait log before choosing one improvement.
options.consequence: The improvement begins with reader experience and checks its operational pattern.
options.application: Staff identify the most repeated concern in reader feedback and check the wait log before choosing one improvement. The improvement begins with reader experience and checks its operational pattern.

options.mechanism: Staff propose one improvement during closing and compare both the wait log and reader feedback before agreeing to try it.
options.consequence: The proposed change must fit both kinds of evidence.
options.application: Staff propose one improvement during closing and compare both the wait log and reader feedback before agreeing to try it. The proposed change must fit both kinds of evidence.

problems.title: A neighborhood café that lends reusable cups
problems.problem: A neighborhood café wants to lend reusable cups at community gatherings and recover them afterward. It has a modest cup stock, washable collection crates, a simple lending record, and volunteers who can share short shifts. The plan concerns a small pilot with no deposit or sales system. Different decisions address separate moments in lending, return, and review.
problems.goal: Make cup lending and return convenient while keeping the available stock and volunteer work understandable.

decisions.question: How should guests indicate that they want a reusable cup?
decisions.context: Guests can make a request at the drink counter, and a request card can pass between the drink and cup stations.

options.mechanism: Guests request a reusable cup at the drink counter, which sends a request card to the cup station.
options.consequence: The cup station prepares for a guest before the guest reaches it.
options.application: Guests request a reusable cup at the drink counter, which sends a request card to the cup station. The cup station prepares for a guest before the guest reaches it.

options.mechanism: Guests collect a request card at the cup station and show it when ordering at the drink counter.
options.consequence: The cup choice is settled before the drink is prepared.
options.application: Guests collect a request card at the cup station and show it when ordering at the drink counter. The cup choice is settled before the drink is prepared.

options.mechanism: A volunteer gathers reusable-cup requests from waiting guests and takes the cards to both stations.
options.consequence: Both stations receive the same choices while guests remain in the queue.
options.application: A volunteer gathers reusable-cup requests from waiting guests and takes the cards to both stations. Both stations receive the same choices while guests remain in the queue.

decisions.question: How should available cups be allocated during busy periods?
decisions.context: There are fewer cups than peak simultaneous requests, but guests can wait or use their own cups.

options.mechanism: Volunteers assign available cups in request order and tell later guests when a return is expected.
options.consequence: The waiting order is clear when stock runs short.
options.application: Volunteers assign available cups in request order and tell later guests when a return is expected. The waiting order is clear when stock runs short.

options.mechanism: Volunteers reserve a small number of available cups for each upcoming service period and take requests within that period.
options.consequence: Early requests cannot consume the whole afternoon’s lending stock.
options.application: Volunteers reserve a small number of available cups for each upcoming service period and take requests within that period. Early requests cannot consume the whole afternoon’s lending stock.

options.mechanism: Volunteers ask guests when they will need a cup and allocate available cups to the earliest stated need.
options.consequence: Allocation follows intended use time rather than request time.
options.application: Volunteers ask guests when they will need a cup and allocate available cups to the earliest stated need. Allocation follows intended use time rather than request time.

decisions.question: How should a borrowed cup be recorded?
decisions.context: A lending record can connect a cup’s distinguishing description with the guest’s chosen return time.

options.mechanism: The volunteer records the cup description and asks the guest to add a return time.
options.consequence: The guest makes the return commitment in the lending record.
options.application: The volunteer records the cup description and asks the guest to add a return time. The guest makes the return commitment in the lending record.

options.mechanism: The guest enters the cup description and return time, and the volunteer checks the entry before handover.
options.consequence: The record is completed by the borrower and checked once.
options.application: The guest enters the cup description and return time, and the volunteer checks the entry before handover. The record is completed by the borrower and checked once.

options.mechanism: The volunteer asks for the return time while handing over the cup and completes both fields afterward.
options.consequence: The handover conversation supplies the record without a separate writing step for the guest.
options.application: The volunteer asks for the return time while handing over the cup and completes both fields afterward. The handover conversation supplies the record without a separate writing step for the guest.

decisions.question: How should guests learn where to return cups?
decisions.context: The café can show a return map on the counter and on small cards beside the cups.

options.mechanism: Guests look at the counter map before choosing a cup and take a return card if needed.
options.consequence: The return route is considered before the loan begins.
options.application: Guests look at the counter map before choosing a cup and take a return card if needed. The return route is considered before the loan begins.

options.mechanism: Volunteers give each guest a return card with the cup and point to the same route on the counter map.
options.consequence: The return explanation accompanies the handover.
options.application: Volunteers give each guest a return card with the cup and point to the same route on the counter map. The return explanation accompanies the handover.

options.mechanism: Volunteers display the return cards beside the cups and use the counter map to answer questions afterward.
options.consequence: Guests can learn the route themselves while help remains available.
options.application: Volunteers display the return cards beside the cups and use the counter map to answer questions afterward. Guests can learn the route themselves while help remains available.

decisions.question: How should a return point collect used cups?
decisions.context: A return point has collection crates and space for guests to pause without blocking the serving area.

options.mechanism: Guests place used cups directly in collection crates while a volunteer checks the crates at intervals.
options.consequence: Return remains quick even when the volunteer is briefly occupied.
options.application: Guests place used cups directly in collection crates while a volunteer checks the crates at intervals. Return remains quick even when the volunteer is briefly occupied.

options.mechanism: A volunteer accepts used cups and places them in collection crates as guests arrive.
options.consequence: Each returned cup receives an immediate intake check.
options.application: A volunteer accepts used cups and places them in collection crates as guests arrive. Each returned cup receives an immediate intake check.

options.mechanism: Guests leave used cups on a return ledge, and a volunteer moves them into collection crates in small batches.
options.consequence: The ledge separates guest handover from crate handling.
options.application: Guests leave used cups on a return ledge, and a volunteer moves them into collection crates in small batches. The ledge separates guest handover from crate handling.

decisions.question: How should returned cups be matched to the lending record?
decisions.context: Cup descriptions in the lending record are sufficient to match returns without storing personal contact details.

options.mechanism: Volunteers match each cup description to the lending record before adding the cup to a return crate.
options.consequence: The outstanding list changes immediately at intake.
options.application: Volunteers match each cup description to the lending record before adding the cup to a return crate. The outstanding list changes immediately at intake.

options.mechanism: Volunteers gather a small crate of returns and then match all its cup descriptions to the lending record.
options.consequence: Recording is concentrated into short batches.
options.application: Volunteers gather a small crate of returns and then match all its cup descriptions to the lending record. Recording is concentrated into short batches.

options.mechanism: Guests point out the matching cup description in the lending record, and a volunteer confirms the return.
options.consequence: Borrowers help locate their entries while volunteers verify them.
options.application: Guests point out the matching cup description in the lending record, and a volunteer confirms the return. Borrowers help locate their entries while volunteers verify them.

decisions.question: How should crates reach the washing station?
decisions.context: The return point and washing station are connected by a short route, and a transfer list can record crates.

options.mechanism: A volunteer takes a crate to the washing station whenever the return point marks it ready on the transfer list.
options.consequence: Transfers follow the buildup of returned cups.
options.application: A volunteer takes a crate to the washing station whenever the return point marks it ready on the transfer list. Transfers follow the buildup of returned cups.

options.mechanism: The washing station requests the next crate through the transfer list when it has room.
options.consequence: Transfers follow the washing station’s capacity.
options.application: The washing station requests the next crate through the transfer list when it has room. Transfers follow the washing station’s capacity.

options.mechanism: A volunteer moves crates at fixed intervals and updates the transfer list at both stations.
options.consequence: A predictable round connects return and washing work.
options.application: A volunteer moves crates at fixed intervals and updates the transfer list at both stations. A predictable round connects return and washing work.

decisions.question: How should cleaned cups rejoin available stock?
decisions.context: Cleaned cups are ready for reuse after the café’s normal washing procedure and can be listed as available.

options.mechanism: The washing volunteer adds cleaned cups to the available-stock list before moving them to the lending station.
options.consequence: The lending team can anticipate the incoming supply.
options.application: The washing volunteer adds cleaned cups to the available-stock list before moving them to the lending station. The lending team can anticipate the incoming supply.

options.mechanism: The lending volunteer updates the available-stock list after receiving and counting cleaned cups.
options.consequence: Availability reflects stock physically present at the station.
options.application: The lending volunteer updates the available-stock list after receiving and counting cleaned cups. Availability reflects stock physically present at the station.

options.mechanism: The washing and lending volunteers count cleaned cups together during the handover and update one shared list.
options.consequence: Both stations agree on the stock change at the same moment.
options.application: The washing and lending volunteers count cleaned cups together during the handover and update one shared list. Both stations agree on the stock change at the same moment.

decisions.question: How should the team handle cups that have not returned on time?
decisions.context: The gathering has an announcement board and several return points, but the team does not track guests individually.

options.mechanism: The team posts the number of overdue cups on the announcement board and directs guests to the return points.
options.consequence: A shared reminder can prompt returns without identifying borrowers.
options.application: The team posts the number of overdue cups on the announcement board and directs guests to the return points. A shared reminder can prompt returns without identifying borrowers.

options.mechanism: Volunteers visit the return points with a reminder sign and then update the announcement board with the remaining overdue count.
options.consequence: The reminder reaches likely return locations before the count is refreshed.
options.application: Volunteers visit the return points with a reminder sign and then update the announcement board with the remaining overdue count. The reminder reaches likely return locations before the count is refreshed.

options.mechanism: The team announces a short return period on the board and gathers updates from return points after it ends.
options.consequence: Guests have a clear shared moment to bring cups back.
options.application: The team announces a short return period on the board and gathers updates from return points after it ends. Guests have a clear shared moment to bring cups back.

decisions.question: How should guests extend a loan during the gathering?
decisions.context: A guest may need a cup longer than expected, and the lending record has room for an updated return time.

options.mechanism: Guests choose a later return time in the lending record and ask a volunteer to confirm it.
options.consequence: Extensions begin with the guest’s expected need.
options.application: Guests choose a later return time in the lending record and ask a volunteer to confirm it. Extensions begin with the guest’s expected need.

options.mechanism: Volunteers offer available later return times from the lending record and let guests choose one.
options.consequence: Extensions reflect the team’s view of future cup demand.
options.application: Volunteers offer available later return times from the lending record and let guests choose one. Extensions reflect the team’s view of future cup demand.

options.mechanism: Guests tell a volunteer how much longer they need the cup, and the volunteer records the resulting return time.
options.consequence: A brief conversation turns the guest’s estimate into a shared commitment.
options.application: Guests tell a volunteer how much longer they need the cup, and the volunteer records the resulting return time. A brief conversation turns the guest’s estimate into a shared commitment.

decisions.question: How should volunteers divide intake and recording work?
decisions.context: Two volunteers are available at busy return points, and either can handle intake or the lending record.

options.mechanism: One volunteer handles cup intake while the other updates the lending record throughout a short block.
options.consequence: Each person can concentrate on one part of the return process.
options.application: One volunteer handles cup intake while the other updates the lending record throughout a short block. Each person can concentrate on one part of the return process.

options.mechanism: The volunteers alternate intake and record duties after each small group of returns.
options.consequence: Both share the two tasks while keeping a clear current assignment.
options.application: The volunteers alternate intake and record duties after each small group of returns. Both share the two tasks while keeping a clear current assignment.

options.mechanism: Each volunteer handles intake and the lending record for a separate stream of guests.
options.consequence: A return stays with one person from handover through recording.
options.application: Each volunteer handles intake and the lending record for a separate stream of guests. A return stays with one person from handover through recording.

decisions.question: How should the café explain a temporary cup shortage?

decisions.question: How should inexperienced players receive strategic guidance?

decisions.question: How should refreshments fit around games?

decisions.question: How should players signal a need for a personal break?

problems.title: Coordinating a community choir’s rehearsals
problems.problem: A community choir is preparing a small program through a series of rehearsals. It has a conductor, willing section leaders, a booking organizer, numbered scores that members may use, and shared practice recordings. The rehearsal room has movable chairs and enough space for short sectional work. Members have varied experience and availability. Musical direction remains with the conductor, and each routine below can operate within any agreed rehearsal schedule.
problems.goal: Make rehearsals easy to attend and prepare for while helping singers use shared rehearsal time effectively.

decisions.question: How should rehearsal dates be chosen from available room slots?
decisions.context: The booking organizer can collect member availability before reserving a sequence of room slots; not every member can attend every date.

options.mechanism: Members mark all workable room slots, and the booking organizer reserves a sequence with the broadest overall attendance.
options.consequence: The schedule follows actual availability across the group rather than relying on a presumed regular pattern.
options.application: Members mark all workable room slots, and the booking organizer reserves a sequence with the broadest overall attendance. The schedule follows actual availability across the group rather than relying on a presumed regular pattern.

options.mechanism: The booking organizer proposes a sequence of available room slots, and members identify conflicts before reservations are finalized.
options.consequence: A concrete draft gives singers something specific to assess while leaving time to correct avoidable attendance problems.
options.application: The booking organizer proposes a sequence of available room slots, and members identify conflicts before reservations are finalized. A concrete draft gives singers something specific to assess while leaving time to correct avoidable attendance problems.

options.mechanism: Section leaders collect their singers’ availability and recommend room slots to the booking organizer together.
options.consequence: The scheduling discussion can consider whether every voice part will be represented as well as total expected attendance.
options.application: Section leaders collect their singers’ availability and recommend room slots to the booking organizer together. The scheduling discussion can consider whether every voice part will be represented as well as total expected attendance.

options.application: Members mark their expected attendance on the shared sheet by the day before each rehearsal. The conductor sees individual updates in one place and can anticipate missing voices before choosing the session’s emphasis.

options.mechanism: Section leaders ask their singers about the next rehearsal and enter section totals on the attendance sheet.

options.mechanism: The organizer sends a rehearsal reminder with an attendance response link and summarizes replies for the conductor.
options.consequence: Confirmation is prompted at a predictable time, making the expected numbers easier to use during final preparation.
options.application: The organizer sends a rehearsal reminder with an attendance response link and summarizes replies for the conductor. Confirmation is prompted at a predictable time, making the expected numbers easier to use during final preparation.

options.application: The organizer sends the numbered score list and digital copies before rehearsal, with matching paper copies available at arrival. Singers can prepare early while anyone who needs paper still receives the same music before singing begins.

options.mechanism: Singers collect the numbered scores from a shared catalog when the rehearsal notice appears and mark receipt on a list.

options.application: Singers collect the numbered scores from a shared catalog when the rehearsal notice appears and mark receipt on a list. Members control when they obtain music, while the organizer can identify gaps before the session starts.

options.application: The conductor demonstrates each entrance and cutoff while singers mark the matching cue in their scores before singing. A written reminder is established before the choir tries to follow the same gesture in real time.
